values: Sova helps AI startups test whether a smaller, adapted model can handle a specific workflow faster and at lower cost while meeting their quality bar.
Name their workflow. Savings and speed are hypotheses until measured.
Hi [name], I saw [specific feature] in [product]. I picked [one repeated task] because it seems measurable.
Show their public product page; do not imply access to their backend.
Here is a synthetic example of [task]. This is the output contract and the failure case we would test.
Label synthetic inputs, recorded runs and actual live output.
We would run your baseline and our candidate on the same held-out requests, measuring accepted answers, p95 latency and total cost per accepted task.
No invented baseline, accuracy or throughput numbers.
Ask for a small next step
Would a 15-minute call to pick one workflow be useful? If it is a fit, we can scope a small paid pilot.
One CTA. Link the video, not five attachments.

Hi [name] — noticed [verified product feature]. I recorded a 75-second idea for testing a smaller model on [task]: [video]. We would compare quality, latency and cost against your current setup. Worth a 15-minute chat? — Aniruddh, Sova
Replace every bracket; send manually after checking contact.
One extra thought on [workflow]: [specific failure mode] may matter more than raw tokens/sec. I would include that in the evaluation. Is [task] something your team is optimizing?
Add a real observation, not a fabricated benchmark.
Would a small comparison on [task] be useful, or is inference performance not a priority right now? Happy to close the loop.
Stop if they decline; record stage and reason.
I share short, measured inference teardowns for AI builders. Want me to send you the next one?
Record an explicit yes, date and evidence. A reply to sales outreach alone is not newsletter consent.
Which task repeats most? Current model and prompt sizes? Request volume/concurrency? Quality rubric? Latency target? Data restrictions? Who owns the integration?
Unknown spend/architecture are qualification questions, not presumed facts.
One workflow, agreed held-out evaluation, current baseline, candidate endpoint, failure analysis and deployment recommendation. Train only if prompting/routing is insufficient.
Agree fee, timeline, permitted data and success criteria before running customer workloads.
P1: clear narrow text task. P2: plausible task with integration or quality questions. P3: complex modality, mature specialist stack, or partner motion.
Analyst judgment, not evidence of buyer interest. Team size is source-reported, not verified headcount.
